page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and a massive 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high allocation of 42.0 GB of RAM per physical core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, though it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance, ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. Advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, are present to support specialized integer and cryptography workloads.

Given the absence of local storage and the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. It represents a qualitative tradeoff, prioritizing massive RAM capacity and high CPU clock speeds over local disk IOPS or high core counts. This profile is highly suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, enterprise applications, and workloads requiring fast single-threaded execution alongside massive memory footprints.
